keyVerseText: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again , I will repay thee.
rootMeaning: The Greek noun πανδοχεύς (pandocheús) originates from the same root as πανδοχεῖον (pandocheîon), meaning an inn or public lodging place that is all-receptive. The literal sense conveys one who receives all comers, emphasizing hospitality and openness to strangers. This root meaning enriches the English term 'host' or 'innkeeper' by highlighting the role as a caretaker of a place designed to welcome and provide for diverse travelers, not merely as a business owner but as a guardian of communal refuge.
usageInScripture: The word πανδοχεύς appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Luke 10:35, where it is translated as 'host.' This single occurrence shows a consistent usage referring to an innkeeper or a person entrusted with the care of guests. The translation 'them to the host' reflects the role of the πανδοχεύς as one who receives and provides for travelers, emphasizing responsibility and hospitality within the narrative context.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πανδοχεύς as one who welcomes all guests enriches our grasp of biblical hospitality, a virtue deeply rooted in Scripture. The term's original meaning as an all-receptive innkeeper reminds believers of the Christian call to open hearts and homes to others, reflecting God's inclusive grace. This role models Christ's own ministry of receiving the marginalized and caring for the stranger. Theologically, the πανδοχεύς symbolizes stewardship and faithfulness in service, encouraging believers to embody Christ-like hospitality as an expression of love and unity within the body of Christ.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 10:35, the Samaritan entrusts the injured man to the πανδοχεύς, saying, 'Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.' Here, the word highlights the innkeeper’s vital role as caretaker and provider, entrusted with ongoing responsibility. The use of πανδοχεύς underscores the tangible expression of mercy and compassion, showing how faithfulness in small acts of hospitality reflects God's kingdom values in practical ways.
